summary: Hi, we’re Team Whispers of Space, and we created an audio drama for kids. Through 12-year-old Tara’s homemade ham radio in Kumbalangi, listeners tune into real NASA NSSDCA missions—like Apollo 11, 12, and 15—turning dense telemetry into unforgettable bedtime stories.
details:
Whispers of Space is a three-part narrative audio mini-series created by Team Whispers of Space for young learners (ages 8–13) and curious space enthusiasts. Set on a quiet rooftop terrace in the backwater village of Kumbalangi, Kochi, the series follows 12-year-old Tara as she tinkers with her grandfather’s vintage ham radio and accidentally tunes into Frequency 1957—a mysterious deep-space channel where silent NASA spacecraft wake up once a year to share their stories.

Through immersive sound design and character-driven dialogue, each episode translates real archival telemetry from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) into vivid, accessible storytelling.

Dense technical catalogs and dry historical summaries often make space exploration feel distant or overly intimidating to children. Ghost Signals bridges that gap by turning engineering milestones into relatable, bedtime-friendly audio adventures. Because it is audio-first and low-bandwidth, it is highly accessible for classrooms, mobile devices, and communities with limited screen or internet access—empowering kids from rural backwater villages to bustling cities to see themselves as part of humanity's space story.

Giving distinct personalities to landers, rovers, and surface experiments transforms static "space hardware" into memorable mentors. Complex concepts like laser ranging, thermoelectric nuclear power, and lunar seismology are anchored in familiar comparisons (fingernail growth, a household light bulb, and ringing a bell). Centering the series in Kumbalangi highlights that curiosity about the cosmos belongs to everyone, everywhere—no telescope or mission control badge required.

Official spacecraft trajectories, mission timelines, coordinates, and instrument logs from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA Master Catalog).

Google Docs and Google Slides for scriptwriting and visual presentation, standard digital audio recording and editing software for voice mixing and radio-frequency sound effects, and large language model assistance for script structuring and brainstorming.
